name: Self-RAG (Self-Reflective Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
executive_summary: Train a single model to decide for itself whether retrieval is even needed, then critique the relevance of what it retrieved and the quality of its own output, using special reflection tokens generated inline.
description: Directly addresses plain RAG's stated pitfall in this catalog — that acknowledging insufficient retrieval isn't automatic and must be separately prompted for. Self-RAG bakes the decision into the model's own generation policy via trained 'reflection tokens': the model decides on-demand whether retrieval would help for the current segment, retrieves only when it judges retrieval necessary, generates while emitting tokens that assess the relevance/support of retrieved passages, and emits a token critiquing its own output quality. Reports outperforming ChatGPT and retrieval-augmented Llama2-chat on open-domain QA, reasoning, and fact verification, with notable gains in citation accuracy for long-form generation.
when_to_use: You control fine-tuning and want retrieval-necessity and passage-relevance judgments built into the model's generation policy rather than governed entirely by prompt-level instructions.
Long-form generation tasks where citation accuracy and avoiding over-retrieval (or under-retrieval) both matter.
when_not_to_use: Working with a fixed, already-trained model with no fine-tuning access — use plain retrieval-augmented-generation's prompt-level insufficiency guard instead.
known_pitfalls: Requires training infrastructure and reflection-token-annotated training data; the specific reflection-token vocabulary is fixed at training time and doesn't adapt to a genuinely novel retrieval-quality signal introduced later without retraining.

primary_source.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection

usage_templates.template:
# At each generation segment, the trained model itself emits:
[Retrieve=Yes/No/Continue] — whether retrieval would help for this segment
# If Retrieve=Yes:
Retrieve passages for: {{current_segment_query}}
[IsRel=Relevant/Irrelevant] for each retrieved passage: {{retrieved_passage}}
Generate the segment conditioned on relevant passages only.
[IsSup=Fully supported/Partially supported/No support] — how well the generated segment is supported by the passages used
[IsUse=1-5] — overall usefulness self-rating of the segment

# At inference, these tokens can be used to filter/rerank multiple sampled generations, not just to produce a single pass.

variables.name: current_segment_query
variables.description: Implicit query for the segment currently being generated

variables.name: retrieved_passage
variables.description: One passage retrieved for relevance assessment

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: This template describes a training-time process (fine-tuning or policy training), not a single reproducible inference call; reproducibility depends on the training pipeline and data, not on prompt text alone.
